input: Research accessible travel destinations for elderly parents

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is domestic or international, and how many destinations to research, determines the breadth of the plan and how deep each option needs to be explored.

Understanding the parents' specific mobility or health conditions directly determines what 'accessible' means — wheelchair access, low walking distances, altitude sensitivity, medical facility proximity, etc.
Budget and trip duration set hard limits on which destinations are realistic and how premium the accessibility accommodations need to be.
The time of year affects climate suitability, crowd levels, and physical comfort for elderly travelers, which can rule destinations in or out.
The parents' interests — cultural, nature-based, relaxing, culinary — shape which accessible destinations are actually appealing vs. merely feasible.
Knowing whether the user is traveling with their parents or the parents are traveling alone changes the level of support needed and the type of destination that is suitable.
The intended output format — a shortlist, a detailed report, booking recommendations — determines how deep the research needs to go and what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Research accessible travel destinations for elderly parents
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate travel destinations that are safe, comfortable, and accessible for elderly parents, taking into account their specific mobility, health, and personal preferences.

questions.title: Are you looking at domestic or international destinations?
questions.description: Clarifies the geographic scope of the research, which determines travel complexity, visa needs, and the range of options to consider.

questions.title: What specific mobility or health needs do your parents have?
questions.description: Identifies the exact accessibility requirements — such as wheelchair use, limited walking, oxygen needs, or proximity to medical care — that destinations must meet.

questions.title: What is the approximate budget for this trip?
questions.description: Sets the financial constraint that filters out destinations or accommodation types that are not realistically affordable.

questions.title: When are your parents planning to travel?
questions.description: Determines the travel season, which affects climate suitability, crowd levels, and physical comfort for elderly travelers.

questions.title: What kinds of experiences do your parents most enjoy?
questions.description: Captures personal interests — such as nature, culture, relaxation, or food — so that accessible destinations can also be genuinely appealing to them.

questions.title: Will you be accompanying your parents, or traveling independently?
questions.description: Determines whether a support companion is present, which changes the level of on-the-ground assistance needed and the suitability of certain destination types.

questions.title: What should the final output of this research look like?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user needs a quick shortlist, a detailed comparison, specific booking links, or a full written report — defining what 'done well' means.
